data.G: PENDING: no candidate program is available in preparation. After research, integrate only measured, correctness-valid improvements, then run the required independent confirmation before selecting final G.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline is a correct, sequential r-c-k kernel that resets C but accesses columns of row-major B with a stride and leaves OpenMP unused. Its three n=1024 samples were 5.9284, 7.5323, and 5.7569 seconds (mean 6.4059 seconds); there are no candidate or confirmation measurements yet. The three trees explore distinct strategies: contiguous row updates, parallelizing the existing dot-product work, and a blocked SIMD microkernel. This is enough breadth without assigning redundant objectives, while the supplied remaining time allows concurrent research and leaves time for integration and confirmation. Require oracle correctness within the fixed tolerance at every checked size before comparing native n=1024 timings; preserve overwrite semantics, signed inputs, the thread budget, and the no-external-BLAS constraint.

children.objective: Explore loop order and contiguous streaming only: zero C once, then evaluate a row-wise r-k-c rank-1 update so the inner c loop accesses B and C contiguously. Focus on compiler auto-vectorization and modest unrolling; do not add OpenMP, packing, or explicit SIMD, so measurements isolate this traversal strategy. A serial implementation remains within the caller's thread budget. Preserve correctness for varying signed inputs and overwrite every output; validate all official sizes and compare repeated n=1024 timings. Record failed variants.
children.subject: Row-major r-k-c streaming and compiler vectorization

children.objective: Explore thread decomposition only while retaining the existing r-c-k dot-product traversal and avoiding loop interchange, cache blocking, packing, and hand-written SIMD. Give each OpenMP worker disjoint output rows or output regions, use no more than min(threads, 8), and avoid parallel-region overhead for small inputs when measurements support it. Verify full overwrite, no races, all oracle checks, and repeated n=1024 timings; record failed variants.
children.subject: OpenMP parallelization of the existing dot-product kernel

children.objective: Develop a cache-blocked GEMM with a register-oriented output microkernel, tuning tile dimensions and, if useful, panel packing or x86 SIMD. Keep output tiles exclusively owned by workers and cap any parallelism to the caller's thread budget; use only ISA code safe for the frozen compiler and target. Do not use external BLAS or specialize to input values. Validate the fixed FP32 tolerance at all checked sizes before comparing n=1024 timings, and record unsuccessful tile or SIMD approaches.
children.subject: Blocked SIMD microkernel and cache reuse
